topic: Emergency fund: many experts suggest saving three to six months of living costs for surprises like a job loss or a broken phone.

episode.title: Coin & Kash: The Broken Phone Surprise

shots.narration: A broken phone shouldn't break your whole money plan.
shots.scene: Bright modern apartment, clean 3D animation, vertical 9:16, no text or lettering.
shots.action: Kash lifts a phone with a visibly cracked, dark screen.
shots.mood: Wide eyes, raised eyebrows, bright friendly colours.

shots.narration: Kash's phone breaks, and she reaches for her savings jar.
shots.scene: Apartment table with an empty glass jar and cracked phone, vertical 9:16, no text.
shots.action: Kash reaches toward the empty glass jar.
shots.mood: Concerned expression, warm daylight, Coin watching sympathetically.

shots.narration: [sighs] Empty—this surprise needs an emergency fund.
shots.scene: Close view of the apartment table and empty jar, vertical 9:16, no text.
shots.action: Kash turns the empty jar upside down.

shots.narration: Coin explains: emergency funds hold savings for surprises, including job loss.
shots.scene: Apartment table with a glass jar and floating pictograms of a cracked phone and closed briefcase, vertical 9:16, no text.
shots.action: Coin points toward the savings jar.
shots.mood: Coin smiling reassuringly, Kash listening closely, warm golden light.

shots.narration: Many experts suggest saving three to six months of living costs.
shots.scene: Apartment table with six miniature illustrative savings jars, each paired with identical house and grocery pictograms, vertical 9:16, no text.
shots.action: Coin sweeps one arm across the jars.
shots.mood: Clear orderly arrangement, bright colours, attentive expressions.

shots.narration: [surprised] Example: monthly costs of one thousand mean three to six thousand.
shots.scene: Apartment table with six illustrative jars containing equal gold stacks, first three on a blue mat and remaining three on a pale blue mat, vertical 9:16, no text.
shots.action: Kash points to the first group of three jars.
shots.mood: Raised eyebrows and a small understanding smile.

shots.narration: Coin shows Kash six jars, each representing one month's living costs.
shots.scene: Apartment table with six illustrative jars and matching house and grocery pictograms, vertical 9:16, no text.
shots.action: Coin lifts one miniature jar beside its matching pictograms.
shots.mood: Cheerful demonstration, Kash smiling with recognition.

shots.narration: Today, write down one month of your living costs.
shots.scene: Apartment desk with Kash's open notebook, simple household pictograms without letters or numbers, vertical 9:16.
shots.action: Kash draws a small house pictogram in her notebook.
shots.mood: Focused expression, relaxed posture, sunny practical atmosphere.

shots.narration: [excited] Next, Kash turns that number into her emergency fund target.
shots.scene: Apartment table with the notebook, empty real savings jar and six miniature illustrative jars in the background, vertical 9:16, no text.
shots.action: Kash places her notebook beside the empty savings jar.
shots.mood: Hopeful smiles, warm light, inviting sense of a next step.

episode.endHook: Next, Kash turns her living costs into an emergency fund target.
episode.description: A broken phone helps Kash discover what an emergency fund is for. Coin explains the commonly suggested three-to-six-month savings target with a simple example, then shares one action to take today. General money education, not personal financial advice.
